initial.reason: Monomer1 is triallyl isocyanurate (three allyl C=C groups) — a trifunctional vinyl-containing crosslinker providing at least three C=C reactive sites to ensure high crosslink density and compatibility with thiol-ene chemistry. Monomer2 is 1,4-bis(2-mercaptoethyl)benzene (two CH2-CH2-SH arms; the SMILES contains the 'CCS' motif twice) — a rigid aromatic dithiol delivering two thiol groups for efficient thiol–ene addition. The pair (multiple C=C in monomer1 and multiple CCS/thiol in monomer2) meets the required functional-group counts and is reactive/compatible for thermoset formation. The aromatic core and multifunctionality are chosen to drive a high glass transition (toward ~175°C) and high rubbery modulus (high Er ≈100) via increased crosslink density and rigidity.

best.reason: Replaced the previous flexible tri-functional design with two tetrakis-aryl cores: monomer1 is tetrakis(4-vinylphenyl)methane (four C=C vinyl groups) and monomer2 is tetrakis(4-(2-mercaptoethyl)phenyl)methane (four CCS ethanethiol groups). Both SMILES are synthesizable and chemically valid. The increased aromatic content and tetra-functionality raise network rigidity and crosslink density to move Tg toward 175°C and Er toward 100. Vinyl (C=C) — thiol (CCS) pairing enables efficient thiol–ene crosslinking; each monomer contains the required reactive groups multiple times to satisfy functionality and compatibility and address the agent feedback.
